topic: GitHub Actions schedule: UTC, delays at the top of the hour, default branch only, and auto-disable after 60 days of inactivity in public repos
text:
Your nightly GitHub Actions job can silently stop running, and nothing fails to tell you.

Four facts from the GitHub docs about the schedule trigger:

• Cron runs in UTC by default (you can set an IANA time zone)
• It only runs from the default branch
• It can be delayed under load; the start of every hour is a named high-load time
• In public repos it's auto-disabled after 60 days with no repo activity

My rule of thumb: pick an off-peak minute like 17 instead of 0, and never let a schedule be the only alarm. If the job matters, alert when it did NOT run.

How do you know when one of your scheduled automations has quietly stopped?
